Reporting Linear Mixed Models

Source: vignettes/articles/reporting-lmms.Rmd
reporting-lmms.Rmd
library(mixeff)

A mixed-model report should describe the observations and grouping units, model specification, estimates, and inference methods. It should also record convergence problems and quantities that could not be computed.

mixeff stores this information in the fitted object. reporting_table() extracts individual sections, and model_report() assembles them with software-version information. This article shows how to use those tables and turn the results into methods and results prose.

Example model

The example uses repeated weekly observations from clinics, with clinic as the grouping factor.

head(clinic_visits)
#>      score week treatment clinic
#> 1 7.330830    0     usual      1
#> 2 7.439355    1     usual      1
#> 3 7.210269    2     usual      1
#> 4 7.199514    3     usual      1
#> 5 6.597443    4     usual      1
#> 6 5.487172    5     usual      1

The analysis estimates average changes by week and treatment while allowing clinics to have different baselines.

Checking the specification

Before fitting, compile the model and read the design audit. This separates formula interpretation from optimization and lets you check the requested random-effects structure.

spec <- compile_model(score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic), clinic_visits)
audit(spec)
#> Audit Summary:
#>   overall [OK]: clean: no warnings or attention items
#>   attention [OK]: no warnings or unchecked inference-critical items
#> 
#> Requested Model:
#>   formula [INFO]: score ~ 1 + week + treatment + (1 | clinic)
#>   model kind [INFO]: linear_mixed_model
#>   distribution/link [INFO]: gaussian/identity
#>   objective [INFO]: exact_gaussian
#>   convergence certificate [INFO]: exact_objective
#>   fixed terms [INFO]: 1, week, treatment
#>   random terms [INFO]: 1
#>   covariance parameter maps [INFO]: 1 map(s)

Fitting and summarizing the model

Fit the model and inspect its summary:

fit <- lmm(
  score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic),
  clinic_visits,
  control = mm_control(verbose = -1)
)

The overview table is a compact first pass over the fitted model: formula, fitting mode, number of observations, fit status, inference availability, and versioned artifact information.

reporting_table(fit, "overview")
#>              field                                       value
#>        model_class                                         LMM
#>            formula     score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic)
#>  effective_formula score ~ 1 + week + treatment + (1 | clinic)
#>         fit_method                                        REML
#>               mode                   confirmatory_as_specified
#>               nobs                                          72
#>         fit_status                          converged_interior
#>          inference             3/3 available fixed-effect rows
#>    artifact_schema       mixedmodels.compiled_model_artifact 1
#>      crate_version                                  1.0.0-rc.5
#>    package_version                                       0.2.0

Data and random-effects structure

The data-design section gives the grouping factors, their number of levels, and rows per group.

reporting_table(fit, "data_design")
#>   group    role group_levels min_rows_per_group median_rows_per_group
#>  clinic unknown           12                  6                     6
#>  max_rows_per_group     status
#>                   6 sufficient

The random-term section records the grouping factor, basis, covariance family, parameter count, and a description of each term.

reporting_table(fit, "random_terms")
#>  term_id original_fragment  group     basis covariance theta_parameters
#>       r0      (1 | clinic) clinic intercept     scalar                1
#>  design_status                                       english
#>     sufficient `clinic` units may differ in average outcome.

Fixed effects and inference

summary() gives a familiar coefficient table. Use it for console review.

coef_table <- summary(fit, method = "auto")$coef_table
knitr::kable(coef_table, digits = 4)
Estimate Std. Error df t value Pr(>|t|) method
(Intercept) 7.6829 0.1965 12.5655 39.1065 0.0000 satterthwaite
week -0.2784 0.0260 59.0002 -10.7280 0.0000 satterthwaite
treatmentcoached -0.8995 0.2623 9.9997 -3.4298 0.0064 satterthwaite

For report assembly, use reporting_table(). The fixed-effect section keeps the estimate, uncertainty, statistic, p-value, method, row status, and reliability label together.

reporting_table(fit, "fixed_effects")
#>              term   estimate  std_error        df  statistic statistic_name
#>       (Intercept)  7.6828778 0.19646018 12.565500  39.106539              t
#>              week -0.2783994 0.02595083 59.000150 -10.727955              t
#>  treatmentcoached -0.8994747 0.26225014  9.999671  -3.429835              t
#>       p_value        method    status reliability
#>  1.665335e-14 satterthwaite available    moderate
#>  1.776357e-15 satterthwaite available    moderate
#>  6.440574e-03 satterthwaite available    moderate

When you need to audit where those rows came from, request the audit view.

fixed_audit <- reporting_table(fit, "fixed_effects", view = "audit")$table
fixed_audit[, c("term", "method", "status", "reliability", "source")]
#>               term        method    status reliability
#> 1      (Intercept) satterthwaite available    moderate
#> 2             week satterthwaite available    moderate
#> 3 treatmentcoached satterthwaite available    moderate
#>                         source
#> 1 fixed_effect_inference_table
#> 2 fixed_effect_inference_table
#> 3 fixed_effect_inference_table

Turning the tables into methods and results prose

For this simulated example, the following prose uses the evaluated fit and coefficient table. An applied report would also describe recruitment, exclusions, and the study design; those facts cannot be inferred from a model object.

We fitted a Gaussian linear mixed model by restricted maximum likelihood to 72 observations from 12 clinics. The model included fixed effects of week and treatment and a random intercept for clinic. Fixed-effect tests used the satterthwaite method. The optimizer reported an interior solution (converged_interior).

Adjusting for treatment, the estimated weekly change in score was -0.278 points (SE 0.026; p < .001). This estimate describes the common weekly slope assumed by the model. The simulated example does not establish a treatment effect in a clinical population.

Fitted variance components

The random-effect table reports fitted variance components, together with their source and availability status.

reporting_table(fit, "random_effects")
#>     group   basis_lhs              kind  variance   std_dev    status
#>    clinic (Intercept)          variance 0.1827548 0.4274983 available
#>  Residual    Residual residual_variance 0.1414236 0.3760633 available

Unavailable results and other qualifications

Build the full model report when you want the section map, software provenance, and list of unavailable or inapplicable fields.

report <- model_report(fit)
report
#> mixeff model report
#>       field                                   value    status
#>     formula score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic) available
#>  fit_method                                    REML available
#>        nobs                                      72 available
#>  fit_status                      converged_interior available
#>   inference         3/3 available fixed-effect rows available
#> 
#> Sections:
#>   overview
#>   model_specification
#>   data_design
#>   random_terms
#>   random_effects
#>   fixed_effects
#>   fit_statistics
#>   optimizer
#>   comparison_ledger
#>   reproducibility
#>   unavailable
#> 
#> Unavailable/caveated fields: 1

The unavailable section identifies missing or inapplicable fields and other qualifications, with reason codes and a record of the action taken.

reporting_table(report, "unavailable")
#>            section             field         status
#>  comparison_ledger comparison_ledger not_applicable
#>                                    reason
#>  no_model_comparison_recorded_on_this_fit

Assembling a report

Use the report sections as the source material for prose:

  • overview records the formula, fit method, observations, fit status, and versioned artifact information.
  • data_design records grouping-unit counts and rows per group.
  • random_terms records the random-effects specification and its design support.
  • fixed_effects records estimates and inference labels.
  • random_effects records fitted variance components.
  • unavailable records unavailable quantities and their reasons.

Use vignette("inference", package = "mixeff") for term tests, contrasts, and model comparisons. Use the introduction vignette’s save-and-revive section (vignette("mixeff", package = "mixeff")) for reports based on saved fits.
